newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller cleared of corruption charge.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller cleared of corruption charge.

text.p: A parliamentary commission on Thursday rejected a second bid to send Turkey's deputy prime minister, Tansu Ciller, to the Supreme Court on corruption charges stemming from her time as head of government.

"Sending Mrs Ciller to the Supreme Court over TOFAS has been rejected after a vote," commission chairman Hayrettin Uzun told reporters. A commission on Monday rejected another corruption charge against Ciller.
Ciller had been facing allegations that she interfered in the sale of state-owned car manufacturer TOFAS to help business allies during her time as prime minister from 1993 until earlier this year.
The commission recommended that MPs vote soon against sending Ciller, Turkey's first woman leader, to the highest court in the land.
The TOFAS allegations constituted the more serious of three charges she faced.

Ciller was cleared on Monday of failing to prevent contract irregularities at the TEDAS state-run electricity company in her time as prime minister. Another commission will rule in the coming weeks on investigations into her substantial wealth.
